title: 2021-11-15 Meeting with Platform team and Core re: Self-Hosted runners
content:
Date

Attendees

  • Ahmad Hamade

  • Tanguy Gouverneur

Agenda

The primary agenda for the meeting was to discuss the utilisation of self-hosted runners on Github and to gauge what expectations and requirements the Core team had on such a solution.

Background

As part of their automated workflows, the Core team conduct performance tests. The Github hosted runners are not particularly powerful machines, see specifications here, but more importantly, they are not always giving the same resources and as such, the tests are not as reliable. To be able to harness the knowledge from performance tests, a stable and reliable environment should be utilised.

Discussion

The Core team would like to have access to a machine that can run their performance test-suite daily. Nightly was initially proposed but the actual time of day is not relevant for the team. It was suggested from the platform team to utilise spot instances to save money and reduce the environmental impact as well. Moving on, it would be interesting to implement a solution based on Green Software Foundation.

Requirements for Core

Availability: ~15 minutes daily (This may very well increase further on, but for the upcoming quarter this should suffice)

Specifications:

A dedicated machine that simulates that it is a Kiosk (CPU, RAM, SSD)
optionally, a dedicated machine that simulates that it is a generic mobile phone (CPU, RAM, SSD)

For a full overview of the hardware requirements for Kiosk, see this article on Toolbox.

The minimum specs on a low end kiosk are:

i5-6300u specs

Constraints

During discussion Ahmad from the platform team informed that a draw back with a self-hosted runner is that GitHub only allows association on a repo-, organisation- and enterprise-level. This means that we would need to setup a runner for every repository that needs one due to being part of the Inter-IKEA org.

This can possibly be solved utilising Terraform Modules as Recommended by GitHub. Ahmad suggested the Terraform module for self-hosted runners on AWS developed by Philips. The “only” draw-back here is that it would utilise AWS instead of Azure. This will be investigated moving forward.

It is possible to run multiple agents on the same machine, but then it’s no longer easy for us to ensure the reliability of the performance test and the resulting data.

Performance

Core has seen issues with performance since migrating from Bitbucket into GitHub. has solved some of these issues and Ahmad suggested some other improvements in relation to caching. Another thing discussed, was to create a Docker Image that would already have Node and Java pre-installed as well as not use a full Ubuntu image, but a smaller one to make the loads run faster and save on run-time.
